title: Transfer-aware acceptance: accept a rule only if it gains on fresh source training items AND a veto-only check on a similar target's training pool (plus a gross-harm screen on generated items) does not show harm
purpose: Purpose 2 (the metric is generalisation: evolve on one benchmark, evaluate on the others). It touches purpose 1 in one place: the generated similar-target panel is the verification side's artifact. Its validity as a stand-in for a real target (parent pass rate, attenuation, same-text null, yield) is the measurable fitness of the "coding rubric". The pilot gives the first measurement of it.
verdict_cn:
结论：能做，代价不高，但作用有限（中等可行）。
意思是：在一个基准（一套测试题）上学到的一条规则，要同时满足两条才接受：
- 第一，在自己这套题里、之前没用过的训练题上，确实涨分；
- 第二，在一个"相似"的基准上检查一下，没有被证明会让它掉分。

实测发现三件事：
1. 规则在相似基准上反而变差（"负迁移"），确实存在。
   - 把 LiveMath（带"以上都不对"选项的数学选择题）的任务说明放进技能，会让 OfficeQA（看财政文档表格回答问题）掉 8.1 分和 9.5 分。这是两个不同时间段分别测的，结果一致。
   - SearchQA（搜索片段问答）的任务说明在自己那里涨 8.8 分，到 OfficeQA 却掉 4 到 7 分（这个还不算有把握）。
   - 原因：这些文字让模型在文档题上也只给一个短答案，不再列算式计算。即使这段文字写在别的基准的小节里也一样。
   - 所以只看"自己涨没涨"不够，而且每条规则都要做这个检查，不能只查标成"相似"的规则。
2. 用模型自动出的"仿 OfficeQA 题"代替真实题来做检查，目前不行。
   - 这次一共跑了 1124 次解题，花了约 287 万 token（token 是模型读写文字的计量单位）。
   - 自动出的 69 道题太简单：空白技能就能做对 89%，69 道里有 61 道两次都对。
   - 效果被压缩到真实情况的四分之一到一半，于是漏掉了上面掉 9.5 分的那个。
   - 它能抓住"答案格式被破坏"这种大问题：一段错放的说明让分数掉了 33 分，被它拦下。
3. 检查的力度有限（每道题跑 2 次）。
   - 用 30 / 60 / 120 道题，抓住"掉 10 分"的概率约 55% / 80% / 97%。
   - 抓住"掉 5 分"只有约 24% / 36% / 57%。
   - 无害规则被误拦的概率在 2% 到 5%。
   - OfficeQA 的训练题总共只有 74 道，最多能抓住约 70% 的"掉 10 分"。
   - 所以逐条检查只能拦住大伤害。"整体不掉分"必须在整版技能层面另外验证。

具体规则：
- 先去掉照抄任务说明的规则（不花钱）；
- 再要求在新抽的训练题上真涨分，并且比无关文字的对照组高；
- 然后在相似基准的训练题上做"只能否决、不能加分"的检查：规则版和原版穿插着一起跑，伤害被证明（单侧 95% 上界小于 0）就否决；
- 另外用自动出题做一个只拦大问题的检查（1% 水平）。
- 举例：一条在自己那里涨 5 分的规则，如果对相似基准无害，接受概率约 79%；如果让它掉 10 分，接受概率只有 18%（用 120 道题检查时 3%）。
- 检查用的题和结果从不给出规则的模型看，只告诉系统"否决或不否决"，不会变成训练信号。

代价：每条通过第一关的规则多花约 50 万到 120 万 token，每一步约 110 万到 360 万。

需要您决定一件事：是否允许用"相似基准的训练题"做这种只否决的检查？
- 如果允许：建议在 SearchQA 上进化，用 OfficeQA 的训练题做检查，论文里把 OfficeQA 标成"检查过的"；泛化的结论只在没看过的 LiveMath、SpreadsheetBench（表格编辑）、ALFWorld（文字版家务任务）上下。
- 如果不允许：必须先把自动出题做难、做准，达到我定的四条标准，才能用来检查。

注意：用 v3（第三版实验）的数据，这条规则不会改变任何结果，因为本来就没有规则在自己那边通过。它的价值要等新版本先让规则在"自己这关"通过才能体现。
evidence:
**Pilot [M]** (OfficeQA as the similar target; window 10/21 01:11-02:37).
- G = 69 generated OfficeQA-style items from the unchanged v3 forward machinery, x 2 runs. R = the whole 74-item OfficeQA training pool, x 1 run. Arms: P (empty scaffold), P2 (same bytes, null), O_home, L_home, S_home, A_O.
- Delivery: 0 unknown cells; 12 truncations, all on R.
- Pass rates on G: P 0.891, P2 0.899, O 0.964, L 0.870, S 0.870, A_O 0.558. On R: P 0.405, O 0.581, L 0.311, S 0.338.
- Saturation of G: under P, 61 of 69 items pass on both runs and 7 fail on both.
- Effects vs P on G, points [95% bootstrap CI]: P2 +0.72 [0, 2.17]; O +7.25 [1.45, 14.49]; L -2.17 [-7.25, 2.17]; S -2.17 [-7.97, 2.90]; A_O -33.3 [-44.2, -22.5].
- Effects vs P on R: O +17.57 [8.11, 27.03]; L -9.46 [-20.27, 0.0]; S -6.76 [-18.9, 5.4].
- Agreement: same sign 3 of 3. G/R ratio 0.41 / 0.23 / 0.32; against E2's earlier R window 0.54 / 0.27 / 0.54.
- Vetoes (one-sided 95% upper bound below 0): G vetoes only A_O (UB -24.4) and misses L (UB +1.78). R vetoes L (UB -0.98).
- The real pool reproduces across windows (E2 10/20 vs E9 10/21): O +13.5 -> +17.6; L -8.1 -> -9.5 (vetoed both times); S -4.1 -> -6.8.
- Mechanism: the answer-only reply share on R rises from 0.23 (P) to 0.59-0.60 under L and S.
- Per-item SD of paired differences: G 0.06 (null), 0.20-0.26 (seeds); R 0.44-0.53.

**Other measured inputs.**
- cal-1 effects vs parent:A, points (SE): parent:B +0.75 (0.99); ids-full +9.25 (2.20); seed-only +8.83 (1.93); seed-rule +0.29 (1.75); seed-rule3 -3.12 (1.79); cand -2.75 (2.31); placebos -3.75 / +3.38 / -10.0 / 0.0.
- Resampled single-look veto, 2 runs per item, at 30 / 60 / 120 items: -10 placebo 0.54 / 0.77 / 0.96; null parent:B 0.043 / 0.034 / 0.021; zero-effect placebo 0.046 / 0.045 / 0.052.
- Two-look veto (60 + 60 items): -10 vetoed 0.933 at a mean of 79 items; null 0.021.
- Training-pool sizes: SearchQA 600, OfficeQA 74, LiveMath 283, SpreadsheetBench 120, ALFWorld 57.
- OfficeQA within-window run variance W 0.081 / 0.095 (v3 training units). Session SD of the seeded OfficeQA parent about 11 points against 2.7 expected from sampling (D12 working data).
- E2 placement: the SearchQA seed gives +6.0 on LiveMath and -4.05 on OfficeQA; under a "General" section it gives +10.8 on OfficeQA.
- v3 proposals: placement 47 local / 1 similar / 1 none. Median lexical overlap with the best-matching card line 0.16; 1-2 of 49 restate their card.
design:
**Notation.**
- p = parent; it must contain all five task-card seeds. r = rule in its actual section. S = source. Q = a registered similar guard target.
- d_i = ȳ_i(p ⊕ r) - ȳ_i(p) over k runs; unknown cells excluded pairwise; truncation counts as a fail.
- Both arms are dispatched in one seeded interleaved shuffle within one window (mandatory: the OfficeQA session SD is about 11 points).
- SE = s_d / sqrt(n).

**Step 0, admissibility (free).** Reject r as a restatement if its overlap with the best-matching line of p ∪ card_S is at least 0.40, or its overlap with card_S is at least 0.60. The v4 "when <condition>" template is required.

**Step A, source gain (D8 C1' per rule or D1 version test).**
- A_S ⇔ LB_S = d̄_S - z_{1-α/m}·SE_S > 0 AND d̄_S > max over placebos (α = 0.05, Holm over m ≤ 5).
- Fresh source training items never shown to a role. Version form: 300 SearchQA items x 2 runs, SE 1.91, so P(A_S) = 0.05 / 0.47 / 0.84 / 0.999 at a true effect of 0 / +3 / +5 / +8.8.
- C1-first: only A_S passers are guarded.

**Step V, veto-only guard on Q's training pool.**
- Single look (pool < 2·n1, e.g. OfficeQA: all 74 items x 2 runs): veto ⇔ d̄_Q + 1.645·SE_Q < 0. P(veto) = 0.05 / 0.29 / 0.70 / 0.95 at 0 / -5 / -10 / -15 points.
- Two looks (pool ≥ 2·n1, e.g. LiveMath or SearchQA, n1 = 60, k = 2): look 1 vetoes if d̄_1 + 1.96·SE_1 < 0. If not vetoed and d̄_1 < 0, add 60 fresh items and veto if d̄_{1+2} + 1.96·SE_{1+2} < 0. P(veto) = 0.02-0.04 for harmless texts, 0.40 at -3.75, 0.93 at -10, at 79-100 items on average.

**Step V_G, gross-harm screen.** On ≥ 60 fresh generated items x 2 runs: veto ⇔ d̄_G + 2.326·SE_G < 0. It catches format breaks (A_O -33: vetoed) and misses content harm.

**Accept** ⇔ admissible ∧ A_S ∧ ¬V_Q ∧ ¬V_G. False-veto budget at most 6%. Joint acceptance (source 300 x 2; guard SD 0.32 at 2 runs, 60 / 120 items; a source-only rule gives 0.836 throughout):
- +5 at home / harmless on the target: 0.794;
- +5 / -5: 0.559 / 0.396;
- +5 / -10: 0.183 / 0.032.

**Firewall.**
- Guard ids come from a separate random stream and are refused by every role prompt builder. Guard cells live in a separate unit. Only the veto bit reaches the gate; the proposer never learns of vetoes.
- The guard is veto-only (reusable-holdout / Ladder logic).
- The guard panel's own numbers are never reported: they are biased by +0.3 to +0.6 points per surviving null rule.
- The guarded target is labelled "guarded"; the generalisation claim is made on unguarded targets. Proposed layout: evolve on SearchQA, guard on OfficeQA-train (the hub of the similarity map), claim on LiveMath, SpreadsheetBench and ALFWorld.

**Rotation.**
- Fresh draws are possible on SearchQA (10 x 60 items) and LiveMath (4 x 60).
- OfficeQA, SpreadsheetBench and ALFWorld reuse their whole pool, which makes them a fixed validation set in substance.
- A generated panel replaces the real-pool guard only after it passes four validity criteria: parent pass rate 0.3-0.7; attenuation λ ≥ 0.6 with the same sign on at least 4 calibration texts; same-text null within ±2 points; at least 60 items per step. v0 fails the first two.

**Rejected variants.**
- "Helps the target" (LB_Q > 0): power 0.35-0.58, it creates a selection channel, and it favours generic text.
- Per-rule non-inferiority at 5 points: a harmless rule passes only 0.37-0.58.
- v3's C4' (sum ≥ 0 on 8-12 items): a harmless rule passes about 0.6, a -10 harm about 0.3.

pilot.result: Completed: 1,124 cells, 0 unknown. (1) Generated OfficeQA-style panel (69 items x 2 runs) vs the real 74-item OfficeQA training pool (1 run), same window. Generated items are saturated: the empty scaffold passes 0.891, and 61 of 69 items pass on both runs. Effects keep their sign (3 of 3) but shrink to 0.23-0.54 of the real effect. The generated panel misses the real -9.5-point harm of the LiveMath seed (UB +1.78, the real pool vetoes it at UB -0.98); it vetoes the format-breaking ALFWorld-seed text (-33.3). (2) Negative transfer is measured: the LiveMath seed costs OfficeQA -9.46 here and -8.11 in E2's window. The SearchQA seed (+8.8 at home) costs OfficeQA -6.76 / -4.05, not significant. (3) The real pool's effects reproduce across windows. Verdict on the pilot: the real target training pool works as a proxy; the version-0 generated panel works only as a gross-harm screen.

risks:
1. Low power for moderate harm (-3 to -5 points) per rule under any affordable design. The per-rule guard is a gross-harm screen; "no drop" must be shown at the version level (D1/D8, about 640 SearchQA items at 4 runs for a 3-point margin).
2. Moot until rules pass at home: on v3's data E9 changes nothing (0 rules accepted).
3. OfficeQA session effects (SD about 11 points for the seeded parent): decisions are valid only with rule and parent interleaved in one window. Cross-window replication here covers only 3 texts and 2 windows.
4. Attenuation of the generated panel rests on 3 seed texts, none of them rule-sized. A rule's effect may vanish entirely into saturation.
5. A guard on one target does not protect another: the SearchQA seed is +6 on LiveMath and -4 on OfficeQA, and its placement can flip the sign. A guard on the hub may not cover its neighbours.
6. Using target training items makes that target "guarded" and, on small pools (OfficeQA 74, SpreadsheetBench 120, ALFWorld 57), amounts to a fixed validation set. This conflicts with the owner's rule unless he accepts it.
7. The guard tilts acceptance toward narrow rules, which are inert on the target. By itself it never shows that a rule transfers.
8. 19 of the 69 generated items were reused from E1. Wikipedia rate limits persist (56 of 191 requests retried).
cost_estimate:
Per-cell real usage, scaffold / seeded parent: SearchQA 1,300 / 3,850; OfficeQA 4,830 / 8,200-8,856; LiveMath 1,520 / 4,410; generated OfficeQA-style 670 / 1,294, plus 2,670 GLM tokens per kept item.

Per guarded rule (the parent arm costs the same once per step):

| guard design | scaffold | seeded |
|---|---|---|
| LiveMath 60 x 2 | 0.18M | 0.53M |
| LiveMath, two looks | 0.24-0.30M | 0.71-0.88M |
| OfficeQA 74 x 2 | 0.71M | 1.21M |
| SearchQA 120 x 2 | 0.31M | 0.92M |
| generated 60 x 2 | 0.08M + 0.16M generation per step | 0.16M + 0.16M |

Per step with C1-first sequencing and a seeded parent: 0 when nothing passes the source test; with 1-2 passers 2.4-3.6M (OfficeQA guard) or 1.1-1.6M (LiveMath guard). Without C1-first, 5 rules per step: 7.3M or 3.2M. For comparison, a v3 screen or confirm round costs 1.2-7.4M on the QA benchmarks.

Optional next pilot (rule-sized texts on a difficulty-calibrated generated panel vs the real pool): about 3-4M tokens.

This E9 work: pilot 2.73M deepseek + 0.13M GLM; the analyses made no model calls.
recommendation:
**Owner decision 1:** may a veto-only guard use a similar target's TRAINING items, provided that target is reported as "guarded" and the generalisation claim is made on the other targets?
- If yes: evolve on SearchQA (600-item pool, so fresh source batches are possible), guard on OfficeQA-train (74 x 2, single look, interleaved), claim on LiveMath, SpreadsheetBench and ALFWorld test.
- If no: the only compliant proxy is a generated panel, and building one that passes the four validity criteria comes first.

**Engineering (v5, after v4 lands):**
1. Apply the guard to every rule, not only `similar` ones, since local text bleeds into other benchmarks. Replace C4' "sum ≥ 0 on 8-12 items" with the veto test. Keep C1-first sequencing.
2. Enforce the firewall as assertions, in the style of `data._refuse_tests`.
3. Add the 1% gross-harm screen on fresh generated items. Use the generator validity criteria as the verification side's fitness, which is the co-evolution measurement for purpose 1.
4. Report per-target test-split paired CIs with guarded / unguarded labels; never the guard panel's own numbers.
5. Optional pilot (about 3-4M tokens): rule-sized texts (the 2 v3 screen passers, cand, 3 placebos) on a difficulty-calibrated generated panel vs the real pool, to measure attenuation for rules rather than whole seeds.

Do not adopt "must help the target" or per-rule non-inferiority at 5 points.
